public_rationale: A study of December 2022 ChatGPT, published February 8, 2023, reported better medical-question performance than GPT-3 and InstructGPT [e1]. That comparison does not establish the extent of overall capability improvement across tasks [e1]. A December 5, 2022 report stated that ChatGPT reached one million users in less than a week [e2]. It provides no comparable usage or press-coverage measurements for earlier GPT-3 releases, so it cannot establish unprecedented attention relative to those releases [e2].
limitations: The medical-question study does not provide a broad, matched capability comparison across several substantial tasks.
The adoption report does not measure both public and press attention on consistent terms across releases.
The claim specifies neither a capability threshold nor the earlier GPT-3 versions to compare.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT was not particularly more intelligent or powerful than earlier versions of GPT-3, despite unprecedented public attention.

statement.excerpt: Although it was not particularly more intelligent or powerful than earlier versions of GPT-3, it caught the attention of the public and the press to an unprecedented degree.
statement.document_title: Large Language Models like ChatGPT say The Darnedest Things

from_speaker: not particularly more intelligent or powerful
attention of the public and the press
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that launch-era ChatGPT offered no substantial overall capability improvement over earlier GPT-3 models, despite attracting substantially greater public and press attention.
The context fixes the observation period from ChatGPT's launch through the post date. Later publications can supply evidence about that period, but later model performance cannot.
Overall capability requires comparisons across several substantial tasks. One improved benchmark or continuing error category cannot settle it.
I read the attention comparison as referring to earlier GPT-3 releases, rather than every previous technology.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations of launch-era ChatGPT and earlier GPT-3 models show little overall capability improvement, while contemporaneous usage and coverage records show unprecedented attention relative to those releases.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations establish substantial, broad capability improvements, or comparable attention records establish that an earlier GPT-3 release attracted equal or greater attention.

This contemporaneous report documents rapid adoption and attributes the announcement to OpenAI's CEO later in the article. It is secondary reporting, used because the attempted primary growth document could not be read; it does not establish an unprecedented level of press attention.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Broad, matched evaluations of preserved ChatGPT outputs from November 30, 2022 through January 9, 2023 and identified earlier GPT-3 models, plus comparable usage and press-coverage records using consistent definitions and release windows.
